correctness.rationale: Vandermonde rank gives equidistribution for at most d distinct translates; fixed CRT laws yield joint divisibility and local masses. Holdridge 2026 Theorem 1.3 eliminates large prime factors separately in each gcd; p^{-2K} controls high valuations, yielding tightness. The finite difference for d+1 consecutive shifts is a bounded nonzero integer and excludes simultaneous divisibility by a chosen prime. Bundled exact checks passed; the infinite proof is analytic.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Inspecting relevant theorem statements found a large-prime estimate and one joint common-GCD coprimality statement; the other sources study single gcd statistics or random integer polynomial expressions, not the full shifted-floor simultaneous GCD vector with its sharp Vandermonde cutoff. A general adelic theorem could yet imply the probabilistic law.

value.rationale: The problem concerns genuinely correlated simultaneous GCDs that share the same integer, so a single common-gcd density does not determine them. A complete joint law for all tuples and a sharp finite-difference failure at d+1 are motivated structural results over infinite parameter families.
